MUQATIL:79:42-46/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r3.claim: Muhammad is a messenger whose task is only to warn those who fear the Hour.

FARRA:v3p234/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r2.speaker: عاصم والأعمش
FARRA:v3p234/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read the active participle munḏiru, without tanwīn.

FARRA:v3p234/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r3.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف وبعض أهل المدينة
FARRA:v3p234/r3.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and some Medinans give munḏiran with tanwīn; both readings are sound and parallel other Qur'anic participles.

TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.speaker: طارق بن شهاب
TAB-FULL:v24p100/r4.claim: Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb says the Prophet continually mentioned the Hour until the warning passage was revealed.

TAB-FULL:v24p101/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p101/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p101/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn Muḥayṣin read munadhdhir with nunation, making the Prophet a warner of whoever fears the Hour.

TAB-FULL:v24p101/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p101/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p101/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn Muḥayṣin read munadhdhir with nunation, “a warner of whoever fears it”; the other regional readers annex it to “whoever,” “warner of those who fear it.” Both readings are accepted.

ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r1.claim: With nunation, mundhir describes present warning or future warning; active participles for present or future are indefinite like verbs. Nunation may be omitted at a resumption, though its meaning remains understood; a past warning is unnunated.

NAHHAS:v5p146/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v5p146/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Ṭalḥa read mundhirun man yakhshāhā with tanwīn; the construct form drops it for ease.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p375/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p375/r1.speaker: من نون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p375/r1.claim: The tanwīn reading treats مُنذِرٌ as a present participle denoting a current warning, supported by the parallel present warning in 21:45.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p375/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p375/r2.speaker: من أضاف
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p375/r2.claim: The construct reading drops tanwīn as in عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم; it may also describe someone who has already warned, like ضارب زيد أمس.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r14.claim: The Messenger is Muhammad, and those who fear it are those warned about the Resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r1.claim: Nadhir can be an indefinite active participle for present or future warning; it takes tanwin as a substitute for a verb, while past warning is not tanwin-marked.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r2.claim: Both with and without tanwin are correct, as shown by parallel constructions involving a completed matter or weakened plot.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r3.claim: Tanwin marks the participle as present; omitting it may be lightened genitive construction, or may refer to past warning already performed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r4.claim: He paraphrases the Prophet as one who warns whoever fears the Hour's coming.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r5.claim: Although the Prophet warned everyone, warning benefits only those who fear the Hour; a warning ignored is as if it had not been delivered.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p203#2/r6.claim: The person who fears the Hour is the one who believes in it.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r3.claim: The Prophet's warning benefits those who fear the Resurrection.

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر والعباس عن أبي عمرو
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r6.claim: They read mundhir with tanwīn; the other readers omit the tanwīn.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r1.claim: Abu Jaafar reads منذر with nunation, ‘one who warns’; the warning benefits whoever fears the Hour’s arrival.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r5.claim: The Prophet was sent to warn those who may be moved to fear by the Hour's terrors, not to teach its date, which would be of no benefit.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r6.claim: منذر may be read with tanwin; the construct reading is a lighter form. Both can denote present or future, while past meaning requires the construct form.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r12.claim: The rebuke means the Prophet has no role in specifying the Hour; his task is only to warn those who fear it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r14.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة وأبو جعفر وعمر بن عبد العزيز وأبو عمرو وابن محيصن والأعرج وطلحة وعيسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r14.claim: Ibn Abi Abla and others read منذر with tanwin; most readers connect it in an إضافة construction to من.

TABRISI:79:45-46/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r13.claim: The Prophet's warning benefits those who fear the Hour; for those without fear it is as though they were not warned.

TABRISI:79:45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر والعباس عن العياشي عن أبي عمرو
TABRISI:79:45/r1.claim: These readers recite “innama anta mundhirun” with tanwin; the other readers omit it.

TABRISI:79:45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45/r2.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد والجبائي
TABRISI:79:45/r2.claim: Their anomalous reading raises “the mountains” in “He firmly fixed them.”

TABRISI:79:45/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:79:45/r5.claim: Tanwin suits an active participle describing present warning, as in the Prophet's statement that he warns by revelation.

TABRISI:79:45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45/r6.claim: Without tanwin, mundhir may be treated as a lightened annexed form or as one who has already warned.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#11/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#11/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#11/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads mundhir with nunation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#11/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#11/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#11/r2.claim: The Prophet's role is only to warn those who fear the Hour; warning benefits believers who fear it, while the heedless act as if unwarned.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r1.claim: The Prophet's task is warning, which does not require knowing the Hour's time; warning is more effective when its time is unknown.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r2.claim: The Prophet warns everyone, but those who fear the Hour are specified because they benefit from warning.

RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p48#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mundhir is normally indefinite with tanwin for present or future action because it stands for a verb; tanwin may be dropped for lightness, while past use requires annexation.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r14.claim: The Prophet warns everyone accountable, but the warning specifically benefits those who fear the Hour.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r15.speaker: القراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r15.claim: The common reading makes mundhir a genitive construction without tanwīn for ease, though its original form takes tanwīn as a future active participle.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r16.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:42-45/r16.claim: Both with and without tanwīn are permitted; several readers recite mundhir with tanwīn, making it accusative in sense as one who warns those who fear the Hour.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.claim: The passage answers those who claim the afterlife involves only spiritual comfort or pain without sensation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:41-45/r5.claim: The Messenger was sent only to warn those who fear the Hour, since they benefit from warning; Abū ʿAmr reads مُنذر with tanwin and normal government.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#6/r1.claim: The Prophet was sent to warn people who fear the Hour's terrors, not to tell them its time; Yazīd and ʿAbbās read nadhīrun with tanwīn.

QASHANI:79:45-46/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:45-46/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:45-46/r1.claim: The Prophet warns only those who believe in the Hour by imitation and therefore fear it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r7.speaker: الجمهور؛ عمر بن عبد العزيز، أبو جعفر، شيبة، خالد الحذاء، ابن هرمز، عيسى، طلحة، ابن محيصن، أبو عمر، ابن مقسم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r7.claim: The majority read منذر in إضافة; the others read it with nunation. Al-Zamakhshari calls nunation original, while Abu Hayyan says إضافة is the nominal default.

SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r1.claim: Most readers use the genitive construct ‘mundhir man’, easing the adjective’s attachment to its object; both construct and nunated forms can refer to present or future warning.

SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز، أبو جعفر، طلحة، ابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r2.claim: ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, Abu Ja‘far, Talha, and Ibn Muhaysin read ‘mundhirun’ with nunation.

SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls nunation the original form and construct an easing; for past warning, he says only the construct works, as in ‘warning Zayd yesterday’.

SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r4.claim: The Shaykh instead prefers the construct as the original because verbal governance comes from resemblance and construct is basic in nouns; he objects that the past-tense claim has grammatical qualifications.

SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:45/r5.claim: The author replies that he need not discuss a disputed grammatical detail when he has stated a position shared by the majority.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r1.claim: The Prophet was sent to warn people of God’s might and punishment; whoever fears God and His warning follows him and succeeds, while rejecters fail.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r4.claim: The Prophet’s mission is to warn those capable of fearing the Hour, not to date it; concealing its time increases the receptive person’s fear, while the heedless become more reckless.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r5.claim: Those without fear receive only the outward form of a warning and gain no benefit from it, whereas the fearful understand and act on it.

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r5.claim: The Prophet says Paradise is entered by one who hopes for it, Hell is avoided by one who fears it, and God shows mercy to one who is merciful.

BURSEVI:v10p256/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r3.claim: The Prophet’s duty is to obey God by warning about the Hour’s nearness and terrors, not to assign a time that was never entrusted to him.

BURSEVI:v10p256/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r4.claim: The phrase can mean either that the Prophet is only a warner, or that he warns only those who fear; the latter limits the effective response, not his mission to all.

BURSEVI:v10p256/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r5.claim: The majority treat “warner of those who fear it” as an adjective annexed to its object for brevity; fearers are singled out because they benefit from warning.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r1.claim: This clarifies that the Prophet is forbidden to disclose the Hour's time, not to mention it: his task is to warn the fearful about its approach and terrors.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r2.claim: On the alternate reading, the Prophet's mission as the final prophet is itself a sign of the Hour, as in the report that he and the Hour were sent like two fingers.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r3.claim: The restriction may limit the Prophet's description to warning rather than teaching the time, or may mean he warns only those who fear; the second matches an immediate reading but is grammatically disputed.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r4.claim: An objection says من يخشى is attached to منذر and outside إنما's restriction; the author questions the objection because it would also invalidate familiar constructions such as إنما هو غلام زيد.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p37#4/r5.claim: On the second interpretation, إنما may simply emphasize the statement rather than restrict it, since restriction seems to serve no purpose there.

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r5.claim: The Prophet is a warner for those who fear the Hour and will guard themselves.

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r7.claim: Because warning benefits those who fear, later suras will continue to explain whom these warnings benefit and how.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p95/r1.claim: The reply redirects their demand for a date toward what matters: the Prophet's task is to warn those who fear the Hour, a ‘wise style’ like the Prophet asking a questioner what he had prepared.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r1.claim: Most readers use an annexed form of mundhir; Abu Ja'far reads it with nunation, making ‘those who fear it’ its object.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r2.claim: The construction implies ‘warner of it, so whoever fears it takes warning’: the Prophet addresses all, but only those who fear the Hour benefit, honoring believers and shaming unbelievers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r3.claim: People are still called to faith and piety despite God's foreknowledge, since that knowledge is hidden from people and an individual's end appears only after death; the theologians call this muwafat.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97#2/r4.claim: The reply addresses the apparent request for timing and their use of delay to deny the Hour: it will occur, and the waiting will seem no longer than part of a day.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97/r1.claim: The Prophet's role is to warn of the Hour's sudden arrival, not announce its date; disbelievers wrongly treat silence about timing as proof against the Hour and assume he knows the unseen.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p97/r2.claim: Innama restricts the Prophet to the function of warning, countering their assumption that he has access to the unseen.

TABATABAI:79:46/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r3.claim: The Prophet is commissioned only to warn those disposed to fear the Hour when reminded; he is not commissioned to disclose its time.

TABATABAI:79:46/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r4.claim: The exclusive warning role narrows the Prophet's task and denies that he knows the date; “fear” is readiness to fear upon reminder, not necessarily existing fear before warning.

BINTSHATI:v1p161/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p161/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p161/r2.claim: Khashya is fear joined with reverence for the feared one, most often attributed in the Qur’an to believers, messengers, scholars, and those hoped to be guided.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r2.claim: The Prophet's warning benefits those who fear Judgment on the basis of arguments before seeing it; he is not responsible for those demanding to witness it first.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:42/r4.claim: The Prophet's task is to warn that Resurrection will certainly come, alert those who fear it, and urge them to prepare, not to announce its date.

QIRAAT-ER:79:45:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:79:45:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:79:45:3#1/r1.claim: Tanwīn makes mundhir indefinite rather than construct-like before man, presenting a general warning role.

STUDYQURAN:79:45/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:45/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:45/r1.claim: The Prophet does not know the Hour or other Unseen matters; his mission is to warn, though prophets also bring glad tidings.

STUDYQURAN:79:45/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:45/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:45/r2.claim: People expect prophets to act as soothsayers, but the Prophet follows revelation and is only a clear warner.
